userStories.title: Build the effectiveness evaluation harness
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a validated evaluation harness and nax context effectiveness eval command before changing classification.

**Motivation** — There is no ground truth for which chunks mattered, and any flatness metric is maximised by a classifier that always answers ignored. The harness is therefore built first, and the classifier is written against it.

**Approach** — Scope-limited deterministic attribution. Classification stays deterministic with no LLM call, preserving the contract stated in the effectiveness.ts module header. Two alternatives were considered and rejected for this spec: an LLM judge for chunks whose scope is too broad to discriminate, and counterfactual attribution from run outcomes.

**Scope** — In: version-1 self-contained labels, validation, per-signal precision/recall/F1, unclear exclusion, constant-ignored baseline, Spearman size correlation, human/JSON output, and exit codes. Out: scope persistence (US-002), scoped production classification (US-003), wrapper removal (US-004).

**Interface** — nax context effectiveness eval [--labels <path>] [--json]. label is followed, ignored, contradicted, or unclear; unclear is excluded from precision and recall. EvalReport exposes perSignal, baseline, sizeCorrelation, scoredCount, and excludedCount. JSON emits exactly one EvalReport to stdout.
acceptanceCriteria: [loadLabelSet] returns one case with the input caseId for valid version: 1 JSON containing one well-formed case.
[loadLabelSet] throws an error naming both caseId and label when a case omits label.
[loadLabelSet] throws an error code distinguishable from schema errors for invalid JSON.
[scoreEffectiveness] returns per-signal precision, recall, and f1 values in [0,1] when 3 of 4 scored cases match.
[scoreEffectiveness] excludes unclear cases from every per-signal precision/recall figure and returns their excludedCount.
[scoreEffectiveness] returns baseline calculated from an always-ignored classifier.
[scoreEffectiveness] returns sizeCorrelation greater than 0.9 when followed occurs only for the longest half of diffs.
[scoreEffectiveness] returns sizeCorrelation with absolute value below 0.2 when followed is evenly distributed across diff lengths.
[scoreEffectiveness] returns perSignal, baseline, sizeCorrelation, scoredCount, and excludedCount.
When `nax context effectiveness eval` uses a fixture whose classifier meets every recorded baseline threshold, then it exits 0.
When `nax context effectiveness eval` receives a nonexistent labels path, then it exits 2 and stderr names that path.
When `nax context effectiveness eval` cannot read a labels file, then it exits 2 and stderr states the read failure.
When `nax context effectiveness eval` receives a schema-invalid labels file, then it exits 2, writes the validation reason to stderr, and does not score a partial label set.
When `nax context effectiveness eval` runs with --json, then stdout is one parseable object including perSignal and sizeCorrelation and has no table rows.
When one label case throws while scoring, then a warning names its caseId and the remaining cases are scored.

routing.reasoning: New validation, scorer/statistics, output contract, and CLI integration.

userStories.title: Persist rule scope as an attribution carrier
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry inherited rule appliesTo globs through raw chunks and persisted manifests.

**Motivation** — The carrier for the fix already exists. RuleSection already inherits appliesTo and StaticRulesProvider already filters by it at selection time. This story threads that same scope through to classification time.

**Approach** — scopePaths needs adding to RawChunk only: PackedChunk extends ScoredChunk extends RawChunk, so the field reaches buildManifest through inputs.packed with no further plumbing.

**Scope** — In: optional RawChunk.scopePaths, StaticRulesProvider population from inherited section appliesTo, ContextManifest.chunkScopePaths, manifest assembly and persistence. Out: Populating scopePaths for providers other than StaticRulesProvider is deferred; those chunks keep today's whole-diff behaviour. No change to how chunks are selected for a bundle. This spec reads appliesTo at classification time and does not alter ruleMatchesScopeFiles or any selection-time filtering. Evaluation (US-001), classification (US-003), and wrapper removal (US-004) belong to other stories.

**Interface** — scopePaths?: string[] on RawChunk and chunkScopePaths?: Record<string, string[]> on ContextManifest. buildManifest maps scoped chunk IDs to globs and omits the map when empty.

**Design note** — static-rules.ts is 583 lines against the 600-line source limit. Keep population minimal; if it would breach 600, extract the chunk-construction block to a sibling module.
acceptanceCriteria: [RawChunk] accepts scopePaths: string[] and accepts chunks without it everywhere accepted today.
[StaticRulesProvider.fetch] returns scopePaths ["src/agents/**/*.ts"] for matching appliesTo frontmatter.
[StaticRulesProvider.fetch] omits scopePaths for a rule without appliesTo.
[StaticRulesProvider.fetch] gives two sections of one rule the rule's appliesTo globs.
[buildManifest] maps a packed scoped chunk ID to its globs in chunkScopePaths.
[buildManifest] omits chunkScopePaths when no packed chunk has scopePaths.
When a scoped manifest is written and loaded, then its chunkScopePaths mapping is unchanged.

routing.reasoning: Optional carrier crosses provider, pure assembly, and persistence using established patterns.

userStories.title: Classify effectiveness from scoped added diff lines
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace whole-diff attribution with per-chunk, scope-limited added-line evidence and gate it through the harness.

**Motivation** — classifyWithTerms marks followed when a 300-character summary shares at least three tokens with the whole story diff. Both operands grow with diff size, so the signal measures diff size, not whether the chunk mattered.

**Approach** — Split the diff per file once per story, restrict each chunk's evidence to the added lines of files its scopePaths admits, and replace the absolute shared-term threshold with a size-independent criterion. Gated by the US-001 harness against the recorded baseline.

**Scope** — In: post-image diff splitting, rename/binary handling, glob scope slicing, added-lines-only evidence, file-path evidence, fallbacks, annotation integration, eval CLI delegation, and fixture gates. Out: The §23 effectiveness-to-scoring feedback loop — a learned per-provider multiplier applied in scoreChunk — is deferred to a separate spec that runs only after this spec's evaluation harness reports whether the new classifier beats the recorded baseline. An LLM-backed judge for chunks whose appliesTo scope is too broad to discriminate is deferred; this spec ships deterministic attribution only. No change to how chunks are selected for a bundle. This spec reads appliesTo at classification time and does not alter ruleMatchesScopeFiles or any selection-time filtering. Carrier creation (US-002), scorer infrastructure (US-001), constant tuning, and wrapper removal (US-004) are outside this story.

**Interface** — splitDiffByFile is importable from effectiveness.ts. classifyWithTerms and buildEvidenceTerms are exported. annotateManifestEffectiveness reads chunkScopePaths and classifies matching added-line slices.

**Failure handling** — No scopePaths fails open to whole diff. Scope matching no diff file is ignored. An unsplittable diff fails open to whole diff and records unknown. A scoring case throw logs warning with caseId and continues. Existing per-manifest read-modify-write catch/log/continue behavior remains.

**Gate** — Scoped fixture sizeCorrelation absolute value is strictly smaller than pre-change whole-diff correlation, and followed F1 is strictly greater than the same report's baseline F1.
acceptanceCriteria: [splitDiffByFile] maps each post-image path to only its section for a two-file unified diff.
[splitDiffByFile] keys a rename section by its post-rename path.
[splitDiffByFile] returns an empty section for a binary-marked file without throwing.
When scopePaths is ["src/agents/**/*.ts"] and the diff only touches src/cli/context.ts, then classification is ignored despite more than three shared terms.
When that scope sees src/agents/acp/adapter.ts and src/cli/context.ts, then it considers only the adapter section's terms.
When scopePaths is absent, then classification considers the whole diff.
When a diff cannot be split into per-file sections, then classification fails open to the whole diff and records unknown for the chunk.
When terms occur exclusively on removed/context lines, then classification is not followed.
When scoped classification is followed, then evidence names a file path from its scoped slice.
When annotation processes a persisted scope excluding all changed files, then it writes ignored and not followed.
When the synthetic fixture is scored, then scoped sizeCorrelation absolute value is strictly smaller than pre-change whole-diff sizeCorrelation absolute value.
When the synthetic fixture is scored, then followed F1 is strictly greater than baseline.f1 in that report.
When a manifest read-modify-write fails during annotation, then annotation logs the failure and continues to the next manifest.
When `nax context effectiveness eval` is invoked with scoreEffectiveness stubbed, then it calls the stub exactly once with the fixture's full case list.

routing.reasoning: Extends the established deterministic annotator across diff parsing, manifest scope data, CLI delegation, and regression gates, but does not alter security or execution lifecycle architecture.

modifiedFiles.reason: Its classifyEffectiveness cases assert whole-diff term-overlap outcomes that scoped attribution deliberately changes; a correct implementation fails them. Replace each with the equivalent assertion through classifyWithTerms plus buildEvidenceTerms, holding scope constant, so the invariant becomes "the same evidence under a fixed scope yields the same signal" rather than "the whole diff yields the same signal".

outOfScope: tuning the classifier's coverage-ratio constant to a specific value is deliberately not pinned here; the constant is whatever value makes AC-10 and AC-11 pass, and the measured value is recorded alongside the fixture.

userStories.title: Retire the test-only effectiveness wrapper
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Delete classifyEffectiveness and make production-path helpers the test surface.

**Motivation** — The wrapper has zero src callers and let the bias survive a green suite by giving tests a path production never runs.

**Approach** — Delete the exported classifyEffectiveness wrapper and use the classifyWithTerms plus buildEvidenceTerms pair production executes. Deletion-only: no new behaviour.

**Scope** — In: wrapper removal, direct/barrel exports, and test migration. Out: scoped attribution (US-003), evaluation harness (US-001), scope carrier (US-002).

**Interface** — classifyWithTerms and buildEvidenceTerms import from effectiveness.ts; classifyWithTerms through src/context/engine behaves identically to direct import; classifyEffectiveness is no longer exported. Removals in this terminal-cleanup story are verified by the build/static gate, not by runtime acceptance criteria. Gate command: `bun run typecheck && bun run lint`.
acceptanceCriteria: When classifyWithTerms classifies a summary against buildEvidenceTerms evidence, then it returns the signal expected by the other effectiveness tests.
When classifyWithTerms is imported through src/context/engine and directly, then both return the identical signal for the same summary and evidence.
When the effectiveness module is imported after US-004, then it has no classifyEffectiveness export.

routing.reasoning: Public API deletion requires barrel and test migration without stale imports.

modifiedFiles.reason: Every remaining reference to the deleted classifyEffectiveness export must move to the classifyWithTerms + buildEvidenceTerms pair US-003 exports; the file cannot compile against a symbol this story removes.

analysis: Existing enhancement. src/context/engine/effectiveness.ts:101-226 pre-tokenizes agent output, the complete diff, and findings in buildEvidenceTerms(), then classifyWithTerms() marks followed on an absolute three-term overlap with the whole diff. classifyEffectiveness() is an exported wrapper with no production caller; tests currently exercise it. annotateManifestEffectiveness() reads persisted manifests, writes signals via per-manifest read-modify-write, and catches/logs failures so annotation cannot stop story completion. RawChunk in src/context/engine/types.ts:356-389 has no scope field; PackedChunk extends ScoredChunk extends RawChunk (src/context/engine/packing.ts:59-64), so an optional field reaches buildManifest without packing changes. RuleSection already inherits appliesTo in src/context/rules/rule-sections.ts:22-89. StaticRulesProvider creates canonical-section chunks at src/context/engine/providers/static-rules.ts:430-450 and can minimally set scopePaths there, but the file is near the 600-line hard limit; extract chunk construction if needed. buildManifest in src/context/engine/manifest-builder.ts:34-105 is pure and persists summaries/tokens/stale chunks, while ContextManifest in src/context/engine/manifest-types.ts:221-236 lacks chunkScopePaths. src/context/engine/manifest-store.ts uses injected dependencies and atomic saveJsonFile persistence; rebuild.ts must be audited too because it reconstructs retained manifest fields. src/context/engine/index.ts is the public barrel. The CLI has only context inspect in src/cli/context.ts, exported by src/cli/index.ts and registered by Commander in bin/nax.ts:1739-1775; eval needs handler, export, and registration with stdout/stderr/exit-code ownership. Existing seams include effectiveness, manifest-store, static-rule-section, and CLI context tests; buildManifest has no dedicated test. Risks: old wrapper assertions deliberately change; absent scope and unsplittable diffs must fail open; unmatched scope must be ignored; rename must use post-image path; removed/context lines cannot evidence followed; output must keep JSON clean; a constant ignored classifier must not pass. Migration is backward-compatible: scopePaths/chunkScopePaths are optional, old manifests and non-opted-in providers use whole-diff behavior. Follow Bun-native, strict TypeScript, _deps, atomic JSON writes, existing best-effort annotation catch, barrels, and source-size limits.
outOfScope: The §23 effectiveness-to-scoring feedback loop — a learned per-provider multiplier applied in `scoreChunk` — is deferred to a separate spec that runs only after this spec's evaluation harness reports whether the new classifier beats the recorded baseline.
An LLM-backed judge for chunks whose `appliesTo` scope is too broad to discriminate is deferred; this spec ships deterministic attribution only.
Counterfactual attribution, inferring chunk usefulness from run outcomes rather than from text overlap, is deferred pending far more stored runs than exist.
Authoring the hand-labelled evaluation cases is a manual data task performed outside any implementation story; stories here are verified against a synthetic fixture committed with the code.
Populating `scopePaths` for providers other than `StaticRulesProvider` is deferred; those chunks keep today's whole-diff behaviour.
No change to how chunks are selected for a bundle. This spec reads `appliesTo` at classification time and does not alter `ruleMatchesScopeFiles` or any selection-time filtering.
No change to `context.md`, to `pollutionRatio`'s formula, or to the `POLLUTION_WARN_THRESHOLD` value.

US-003 only: the classifier's coverage-ratio constant is not pinned to a specific value. It is whatever value makes US-003's two fixture-scored ACs pass, and the measured value is recorded alongside the fixture.
